contract: The server's self-description in /api/cluster/info (published Server 2.11.7 HealthController::clusterInfo) and the activity result read that capabilities.workflow_activity_result_inspection advertises, over raw HTTP in a fresh namespace. Published PHP answers the recorded version shape, capabilities, structural limits and discovery paths, carries its SDK, client and topology manifests, and reads an activity result as pending, then available with its result envelope, and 404 activity_not_found for an activity the run does not have. Native answers the same, except the reviewed native_differences: it advertises no manifest it does not publish, no response compression, no diagnostics view and no external payload transaction limit, and names every member it leaves out in native_unqualified. Embedded applications have no HTTP cluster info.

client_ranges.reason: Native states the ranges its installed qualification supports, from one source for both members (server#1005). sdk-php >=3.8.1: 3.8.0 lost activity claims with heartbeat_timeout under lease maintenance (server#985), fixed in 3.8.1; 3.8.3 passed installed acceptance against native 3.0.4 (https://github.com/durable-workflow/sdk-php/pull/243#issuecomment-6612840439). sdk-python >=2.13.0: 2.13.0 passed installed acceptance against native 3.0.1 (https://github.com/durable-workflow/sdk-python/issues/228, sdk-python#168). sdk-rust >=4.10.3: 4.10.2 failed native describe parity (server#967, fixed by server#968 in 3.0.2); 4.10.3 declares and is qualified on native from 3.0.2 (https://github.com/durable-workflow/sdk-rust/pull/160, harness sdk-rust#155). cli >=2.0.0,<3.0.0: the Rust CLI ships as a 2.x minor (cli#72); its raw worker commands need native 3.1.0 (server#1001). Each upper bound is the next major.

capabilities.child_workflow_start_turn.reason: Native serves start_child_workflow await: "started", a parent turn when the child start commits (Server #966); published PHP 2.x has no such mode.

native_client_compatibility.reason: Native's client_compatibility (server#1005) cites only protocols it serves beside the block: the auth composition contract, the control plane with its request contract, and worker protocol 1.20. Published PHP's block also cites the skew refusal matrix and five worker_protocol external execution contracts, which native does not publish; the CLI checks every protocol the block requires, so native must not cite them.
